Let $\vx_t$ be a zero-mean i.i.d. random vector sequence, and consider the expression $\mathbb{E}\left[\text{Tr}(\vy_{t}\vx_{t+j}^T\vx_{k+j}\vy_{k}^T)\right]$. Which of the following is equivalent to this expression using properties of trace and vectorization?

A. $\mathbb{E}\left[\text{Tr}((\vx_{t+j}\vy_t^T)_v^T (\vx_{k+j}\vy_k^T)_v)\right]$  
B. $\mathbb{E}\left[\text{Tr}(\vx_{t+j}\vy_t^T \vy_k^T\vx_{k+j}^T)\right]$  
C. $\text{Tr}\left[\text{Cov}(\vx_{t+j}, \vy_t)\right]$  
D. $\mathbb{E}\left[\|\vx_{t+j}\|^2\|\vy_t\|^2\right]$  
E. $\text{Cov}\left(\text{Tr}(\vx_{t+j}\vy_t^T), \text{Tr}(\vx_{k+j}\vy_k^T)\right)$  
F. $\mathbb{E}\left[\vy_t^T\vx_{t+j}^T\vx_{k+j}\vy_k\right]$  
G. $\mathbb{E}\left[\text{Tr}(\vx_{t+j}\vx_{k+j}^T)\right]\mathbb{E}\left[\text{Tr}(\vy_t\vy_k^T)\right]$  
H. $\text{Tr}\left[\mathbb{E}(\vx_{t+j}\vx_{k+j}^T)\right] + \text{Tr}\left[\mathbb{E}(\vy_t\vy_k^T)\right]$  
I. $\mathbb{E}\left[\text{Tr}(\vy_t\vy_k^T)\text{Tr}(\vx_{t+j}\vx_{k+j}^T)\right]$  
J. $\text{Var}(\vx_{t+j})\text{Var}(\vy_t)$
assistant
Answer: \boxed{A}

A prosecutor brings a case against a defendant for a felony that requires proof of recklessness—specifically, conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk. The defendant offers testimony that he was so intoxicated at the time that he was unaware of any risk and could not form the conscious disregard required. The trial court excludes this evidence. On appeal, the defendant argues the exclusion violated his due process rights. How should the appellate court rule under the Model Penal Code framework?

A. The evidence must be admitted because due process requires all defenses to be heard.  
B. The exclusion is unconstitutional because it prevents the defendant from disproving an element of the crime.  
C. The court must allow the evidence if it could create reasonable doubt.  
D. The exclusion is proper because the Model Penal Code bars using intoxication to negate recklessness.  
E. The defendant has a constitutional right to present a defense, so the conviction must be reversed.  
F. The evidence should be admitted only if the intoxication was involuntary.  
G. The jury must be instructed that intoxication negates recklessness as a matter of law.  
H. The prosecution must prove sobriety as part of its case.  
I. The court must allow the defense unless the statute explicitly prohibits it.  
J. The defendant can still be convicted of negligence even if recklessness is unproven.
assistant
Answer is \boxed{D}.

A state legislature passes a law requiring all landlords who accept Section 8 vouchers to adopt a uniform screening process approved by the state housing authority, arguing it reduces discrimination and promotes housing stability. A landlord who participates in the program sues, claiming the state law conflicts with federal law. Which of the following provides the strongest basis for invalidating the state law under federal law?

A. The state law violates the landlord’s First Amendment right to association.  
B. The Fair Housing Act preempts any state law regulating tenant screening.  
C. The state law imposes an unconstitutional condition on the receipt of federal benefits.  
D. Federal law explicitly reserves tenant selection to the owner, and the state law directly contradicts that allocation of authority.  
E. The Tenth Amendment prohibits states from regulating federally funded housing programs.  
F. The state law discriminates against voucher holders by treating them differently.  
G. The landlord has a property right in the federal subsidy that cannot be burdened by state regulation.  
H. The Supremacy Clause invalidates all state laws affecting federally assisted housing.  
I. The state law increases administrative costs, making participation economically unfeasible.  
J. The public housing agency has not consented to state interference in its contracts.

A university student consents to a campus security officer searching her dorm room for stolen property. The officer, accompanied by the student, finds no stolen items but observes drug paraphernalia in plain view on a desk. The officer then calls local police, who arrive and seize the items and arrest the student. Later, the student moves to suppress the evidence, arguing the campus officer lacked authority to conduct searches under the Fourth Amendment. How should the court rule?

A) Suppress the evidence, because campus security is always a state actor bound by the Fourth Amendment  
B) Deny suppression, because the search was based on voluntary consent  
C) Suppress the evidence, because no warrant was obtained  
D) Deny suppression, because private individuals are not bound by the Fourth Amendment  
E) Suppress the evidence, because the scope of consent was limited to stolen property  
F) Deny suppression, because the plain view doctrine applies regardless of who conducted the initial search  
G) Suppress the evidence, because campus officers require police oversight  
H) Deny suppression, because university housing has a reduced expectation of privacy  
I) Suppress the evidence, because the officer exceeded the bounds of reasonable search  
J) Deny suppression, because the discovery was inadvertent and lawful

A federal statute prohibits the use of literacy tests in all state-administered congressional elections, regardless of how the tests are administered or whether discriminatory intent is shown. The statute is challenged as unconstitutional. Opponents argue that Congress lacks authority to enact such a blanket prohibition. Which of the following best explains the strongest constitutional argument supporting the opponents’ position?

A. The Fourteenth Amendment only authorizes Congress to remedy proven cases of racial discrimination in voting, not to eliminate neutral qualifications like literacy tests.  
B. Article I, Section 2 and the Seventeenth Amendment vest states with authority to set voter qualifications, and Congress may only modify them through constitutional amendments.  
C. The Supreme Court has never ruled on the constitutionality of literacy tests, making any federal restriction premature.  
D. Literacy tests are explicitly protected by the First Amendment right to free speech and expression.  
E. The Tenth Amendment reserves all election procedures to the states, leaving Congress with no role in regulating elections.  
F. The Fifteenth Amendment applies only to race-based discrimination, not educational qualifications.  
G. Congress may regulate the "manner" of elections under Article I, Section 4, but only if states fail to comply with federal standards.  
H. The Equal Protection Clause does not apply to voter eligibility criteria.  
I. The Voting Rights Act already provides sufficient remedies for discriminatory administration of tests.  
J. States have a fundamental right to ensure voter competence through educational requirements.

During a molecular cloning experiment, a student anneals the following oligonucleotides to form a double-stranded DNA fragment for ligation into a plasmid vector:  
Top: 5′-CCGGGCCTCCGGACAACCCCTTGCAAAGCCAGAACCAC-3′  
Bottom: 5′-CCGGGTGGCTCTGACAGTTGACAGCTCGTTGACAGGC-3′  
After transformation, no colonies are observed. Analysis reveals that the annealed product lacks cohesive ends compatible with the vector. Which of the following best explains the failure of ligation?

A. The two strands are not complementary and cannot form a stable duplex.  
B. The sequences contain internal ribosome binding sites that inhibit replication.  
C. The duplex lacks restriction enzyme recognition sites used for cloning.  
D. The top and bottom strands have mismatched overhangs due to asymmetric design.  
E. The sequences are self-complementary and form hairpins instead of duplexes.  
F. The strands are of unequal length, preventing complete hybridization.  
G. The duplex contains a frameshift mutation that disrupts the origin of replication.  
H. The sequences are derived from a eukaryotic promoter and are toxic in bacteria.  
I. The bottom strand is written in the 3′ to 5′ direction, making it incompatible.  
J. The duplex has blunt ends, but the vector requires sticky ends.
assistant
Answer: D
